statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-4565: the pure-Python backend of protobuf recurses once per nested group, nested message or SGROUP tag, so untrusted data with enough of them exceeds the Python recursion limit and crashes the application with a RecursionError (https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-8qvm-5x2c-j2w7). Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/commit/17838beda2943d08b8a9d4df5b68f5f04f26d901. Debian fixed it for trixie in protobuf 3.21.12-11+deb13u1, whose changelog reads "Fix CVE-2025-4565: data containing an arbitrary number of recursive groups, recursive messages or a series of SGROUP tags can be corrupted by exceeding the Python recursion limit (closes: #1108057)" (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-4565). The DHI protobuf packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie protobuf. The current-scheme builds start at 3.21.12-11+deb13u1, used as the fixed version here, which is built from Debian's 3.21.12-11+deb13u1 security update; it is the only protobuf version now published in the DHI Debian repository (libprotobuf32t64, libprotobuf-lite32t64, libprotoc32t64, protobuf-compiler and python3-protobuf with their -dbgsym packages, plus libprotobuf-dev and libprotoc-dev, for amd64 and arm64).
